أَمِرٌ : see إِمَّرٌ. ＝
-A2- (assumed tropical:) Multiplied; or become many, or much, or abundant. (M, K.) [See أَمِرَ.] You say زَرْعٌ أَمِرٌ (assumed tropical:) Abundant seed-produce. (Lh, M.) ―
-b2- (assumed tropical:) A man whose beasts have multiplied, or become many or abundant. (M.) (assumed tropical:) A man blessed, or prospered, (Ibn-Buzurj, M, K, *) in his property: (M:) fem. with ة. (Ibn-Buzurj.) And with ة, (assumed tropical:) A woman blessed to her husband [by her being prolific]: from the signification of كَثْرَةٌ. (M.) ＝
-A3- (assumed tropical:) Severe; distressful; afflictive. (TA.) [See also إِمْرٌ.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
